questions.q: What does Lowndes suggest at an event to skip an awkward start?
a: Ask the host to introduce you
Walk up and offer a compliment
Wait for the other person to speak
Hand out your business card
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends having the host introduce you so you both share a connection.

a: Showing preparation with information you found
Carrying notes into every conversation
Bringing a small gift for the host
Practicing your introduction in advance
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes using research about someone to show preparation, especially online.

a: Matching their movements and vocabulary
Repeating their opinions back to them
Copying their accent on purpose
Mirroring their clothes and style
questions.why: Lesson 2 says matching gestures and using similar words makes people feel comfortable.

questions.q: How can you show someone you are on the same page?
a: Refer to the two of you as we and us
Interject only with short affirmations
Change the subject to shared news
Agree with everything they say
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests using we and us language to create an in-group feeling.

questions.q: How should praise change as you get to know someone?
a: It should become more specific and frequent
It should become rarer and more formal
It should focus mainly on appearance
It should be given only in private
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the closer you are to someone, the more detailed your praise can be.
